- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for high-peak periods.
- After a spike, model tends to overshoot downward; apply a soft decay correction (e.g., 10–15% reduction in 2–3 days) to avoid premature troughs.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — forecast should be anchored to recent 7–14 day average, not 30-day trend.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize the momentum; add a 1–2 day lag correction to downward moves.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates the depth of corrections after spikes — adjust downward by 3–8% for periods with sustained low sentiment or policy-driven declines.
- If sentiment history is all 0.00, avoid overfitting to recent highs; use 14-day rolling average as baseline for correction.
